beats.t: Nothing had been going Yeoni’s way lately. One unlucky day would have been easy enough to shrug off, but little things had been going wrong for days.
That morning was no different. There had definitely been three alarms: 7:10, 7:15, and 7:20. Yeoni had even given each one a proper name.
[ Get up ]   [ Seriously, get up ]   [ Keep this up and your life is over ]
Not one had rung. By the time Yeoni opened her eyes, the light through the curtains was already yellow. Exactly the color of being late.

Her phone was at one percent. The charger sat neatly in the outlet; the loose end was the one for her phone. An unfamiliar notification glowed on the lock screen. [ Fortune damage detected · Turn off notifications? ] Assuming it was an ad, Yeoni swiped it away.
…You cutting me off too?
The charger gave no answer. That day, everything in the world seemed to be quietly turning its back on Yeoni alone.
The sock on the left was white; the one on the right, gray. Even the patterns were different. Yeoni stared down for about three seconds.
…They say mixing and matching is fashionable these days.
Yeoni decided to stay positive. It was the only way she knew to get through bad luck.
The problem was the bus. She tapped her card. Beep. Please try again.
She tapped again. Beep, please try again. Once more. Beep, please try again. The people behind her watched without a word.
(That silence was the worst part.) …You worked fine yesterday.
The card finally worked on the fourth tap, but something between them had already cracked. Yeoni rated it in her head.
(Transit card: one star. Reason: four attempts to work. Would not buy again.)
At lunch, she bought a tuna-mayo rice triangle. The moment she unwrapped it, it fell face-first onto the floor. Scattered rice and half-stripped seaweed made a sorry sight.
(It looked unable to accept its fate.) …Sorry. You were good tuna mayo.
She bought another and kept hold of it. But the first bite set her mouth on fire. Spicy pork. The wrapper clearly said tuna mayo.
Seriously? Even the rice triangles are lying to me now?
The rice triangle said nothing. Naturally. It was a rice triangle.
Tuna mayo outside, spicy pork inside. That's false advertising. I'm filing a consumer complaint.
Up to that point, it was funny. The sort of day a friend would answer with, 'LOL, what's wrong with you today?'
A few days later, it stopped being funny.
Her part-time job interview was canceled that morning. Her assignment file broke just before submission. Her delivery went to another building. The café coupon she tried to use had expired yesterday.
Important messages failed to send. Apologies were always a step late, and words meant to help came across all wrong.
Once, three dots flickered in the reply window beneath the apology she had sent first. Something seemed about to arrive, then quietly vanished.
Yeoni stared at the place where the dots had been, then turned her phone facedown.
Darkness settled over the upturned phone. Yeoni pulled the blanket to her nose. It was a night when no one was to blame, yet she kept feeling sorry.
…Why does everything keep going wrong? Did I do something?

At first she laughed it off as coincidence. But when coincidences pile up for days, the back of your neck goes cold, as though someone is standing behind you. Days begun with a joke kept turning into days spent searching for excuses.
Even so, Yeoni didn't want to believe in fate. Fate was far too convenient a word.
Fail, and it's fate. Break up, and we weren't meant to be. Run late, and it wasn't the right time. Those words always leave me standing in the same place.
They made things easy to explain. They did nothing to ease her heart.
That night, Yeoni peeled off the wet socks, tossed them aside, and collapsed onto the bed. Enough thinking about today.
Today was… one for the history books.
Battery: four percent. As she reached for the charger, the screen lit up by itself.
…What?
An unfamiliar app sat in the middle of her home screen. A black night sky, a door drawn in moonlight, a tiny star. And two words.
〈  Code Destiny  〉
Did I… install this?
She had no memory of it. When she held it down to delete it, the screen answered.

[ This app cannot be deleted. ]
[ This app is connected to destiny. ]
Apps these days have some serious nerve.
I never paid, but I can't get a refund or delete it. Five stars for sheer nerve.
She checked Settings. It wasn't in the app list or storage. Yet there it sat on her home screen, brazen as anything, as though it had always belonged there.
Then the notification she'd swiped away that morning returned.
[ Damage to user fortune detected ] [ Luck leaking · Bond code partially damaged · Wealth code leaking abnormally ]
[ User: Yeoni ]  [ Age: 23 ]  [ Day Master candidate: 乙 ]  [ Day Pillar code: 乙亥 ]
How… how do you know my name and age?
[ The universe has always known. ]
That makes it even creepier!
Enough. Where's customer service? Put me through to a person. Now.

[ Customer support: The universe ]
[ Agents: None · Your place in the queue: ∞ ]
[ 1 complaint received · Transit card · One star ] [ Reason: four attempts to work · Awaiting resolution ]
I only said that in my head!
Yeoni threw the phone onto her pillow. It bounced twice, then lit up again.
[ Begin destiny restoration? ]     [ YES ]     [ Later ]
Naturally, Yeoni pressed [Later]. The screen changed.
[ There is no later. ]
…Then why did you ask?
[ YES ]     [ YES ]
That isn’t a choice. That’s a kidnapping notice.

[ Terms of Service, Article 1 ]
[ By being born, the user has already agreed to all provisions. ]
A tarot card rose above the screen. Against a black background stood a moonlit door, a little flower at its foot. Beneath it were the words [ THE DOOR ].
Is that… even a tarot card?
The door in the card opened. Creeeeak. The sound came from her room, not her phone.
A real door of moonlight stood in the air before her bed. Beyond the crack, an unfamiliar night sky swirled.
This is… still my room, right?

Instead of an answer, cards poured from the doorway: the Star, the Moon, the Sun, the Wheel of Fortune. Her assignment, an inside-out umbrella, and half-finished cup noodles spun around the room. Only a facedown Star card beside the umbrella floated still.
My assignment, my umbrella, my noodles… Actually, forget the noodles!
[ Tarot gate open ]  [ Connecting to the fortune world ]  [ River of Saju coordinates confirmed ]
I said close! What river? This is a studio apartment!
[ Converting initial avatar ]
Light burst from the doorway. Yeoni held on to the headboard until the very end. It was less loyal than she had hoped. Snap.
Traitor!
Yeoni was sucked straight through the tarot door.
Beyond it lay endless night. Night above, night below. Constellations flowed like a river, while countless tarot cards circled her and whispered. Choice. Fall. Beginning. Transformation.
[ Destiny code connection complete ]  [ Entering the damaged fortune world. ]
I never agreed to—
